---
title: "Vestfold Hills: sight lines and midnight sun"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6, out.width = "100%")
library(aspersions)
library(gdalraster)
library(ximage)
## The Reference Elevation Model of Antarctica (REMA v2) as one GDAL data source: a VRT of
## the 2 m tiles with external overviews (10 m, 32 m, 100 m, 500 m, 1 km), so any area at
## any resolution reads only what it needs. See https://github.com/mdsumner/rema-ovr
dsn <- Sys.getenv("ASPERSIONS_REMA_DSN",
                  "/vsicurl/https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mdsumner/rema-ovr/main/REMA-2m_dem_ovr.vrt")
set_config_option("GDAL_DISABLE_READDIR_ON_OPEN", "EMPTY_DIR")
## the 2 m, 10 m and 32 m levels are in a public S3 bucket: read it anonymously
set_config_option("AWS_NO_SIGN_REQUEST", "YES")
set_config_option("AWS_REGION", "us-west-2")
ok <- tryCatch({ ds <- new(GDALRaster, dsn); ds$close(); TRUE }, error = function(e) FALSE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = ok)
```

```{r offline, eval = !ok, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat("> The REMA data source could not be reached when this page was built, so the code below is shown but not run.\n")
```

The Vestfold Hills are a low, ice-free coastal oasis in East Antarctica, about 400 square kilometres of
rocky hills, fjords and lakes between the ice sheet and the sea. Davis station sits on their western
shore. This page reads the terrain straight from the Reference Elevation Model of Antarctica (REMA)
with GDAL, then asks two questions of it: what can be seen from a hill near the station, and where the
low summer sun reaches the ground.

## Reading REMA

One data source covers the continent. It's a GDAL VRT of the 2 m REMA tiles with overviews at 10 m, 32 m,
100 m, 500 m and 1 km. GDAL's warper picks the right level for the resolution asked for and reads
only the bytes it needs, so a 40 km box at 20 m costs about the same as a small box at full detail. The
same source drives a browser explorer, <https://mdsumner.github.io/rema-ovr/>.

```{r read}
dsn
## the full-resolution levels live in a public bucket, read without credentials
set_config_option("AWS_NO_SIGN_REQUEST", "YES")

## warp a box of REMA in Antarctic polar stereographic (EPSG:3031) at `res` metres
read_rema <- function(extent, res) {
  tf <- tempfile(fileext = ".tif")
  warp(dsn, tf, t_srs = "EPSG:3031",
       cl_arg = c("-te", extent[1], extent[3], extent[2], extent[4], "-tr", res, res, "-r", "bilinear"),
       quiet = TRUE)
  ds <- new(GDALRaster, tf)
  on.exit(ds$close())
  read_ds(ds)
}

davis <- c(2302286, 490792)                        # Davis station, EPSG:3031
box <- c(2289000, 2330000, 462000, 503000)        # the Vestfold Hills, 41 km square
vh <- read_rema(box, 20)
attr(vh, "gis")$dim
```

`read_ds()` gives the heights with their georeferencing attached, and both ximage and aspersions take
that directly.

```{r overview}
relief <- hcl.colors(64, "Grays")
ximage(vh, col = relief, asp = 1, axes = FALSE)
points(davis[1], davis[2], pch = 21, bg = "orangered", cex = 1.4)
```

## What can be seen from a hill near the station

Take the highest ground within 3 km of Davis and stand on it, with the eye at 2 m.

```{r lookout}
z <- matrix(vh, attr(vh, "gis")$dim[2], byrow = TRUE)
ex <- attr(vh, "gis")$bbox[c(1, 3, 2, 4)]
xs <- seq(ex[1] + 10, by = 20, length.out = ncol(z))
ys <- seq(ex[4] - 10, by = -20, length.out = nrow(z))
d <- sqrt(outer((ys - davis[2])^2, (xs - davis[1])^2, "+"))
k <- which(d < 3000 & z == max(z[d < 3000], na.rm = TRUE), arr.ind = TRUE)[1, ]
lookout <- c(xs[k[2]], ys[k[1]])
lookout
z[k[1], k[2]]

v <- viewshed(vh, xy = lookout, eye = 2)
v
ximage(vh, col = relief, asp = 1, axes = FALSE)
ximage(v$visible, extent = v$extent, add = TRUE,
       col = c("transparent", adjustcolor("gold", 0.7)), breaks = c(-1, 0.01, 2))
points(lookout[1], lookout[2], pch = 21, bg = "orangered", cex = 1.4)
```

The skyline from the lookout comes out of the same calculation:

```{r skyline, fig.height = 3.5}
par(mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1))
plot(v$skyline, type = "l", xaxt = "n", xlab = "azimuth (degrees from grid north)",
     ylab = "horizon (degrees)")
axis(1, at = seq(0, 360, by = 90))
abline(h = 0, lty = 3)
```

### In detail: 2 m near the lookout

The full-resolution tiles come through the same source. Here a 4 km square around the lookout is read at 2 m,
with the 20 m grid behind it for the terrain further out. The near grid is two million cells, so four million
triangles.

```{r detail}
near_box <- c(lookout[1] - 2000, lookout[1] + 2000, lookout[2] - 2000, lookout[2] + 2000)
near <- read_rema(near_box, 2)
vn <- viewshed(near, xy = lookout, eye = 2, far = z, far_extent = ex)
vn
ximage(near, col = relief, asp = 1, axes = FALSE)
ximage(vn$visible, extent = vn$extent, add = TRUE,
       col = c("transparent", adjustcolor("gold", 0.7)), breaks = c(-1, 0.01, 2))
points(lookout[1], lookout[2], pch = 21, bg = "orangered", cex = 1.4)
```

## Midnight sun

Davis is at 68.6 degrees south, inside the Antarctic Circle: around midsummer the sun doesn't set, and
around midwinter it doesn't rise. Polar stereographic grid north isn't true north. At any point,
true north points directly away from the pole, so the grid azimuth of true north is the longitude, about
78 degrees here. That's the `convergence` argument.

```{r sun-position}
lonlat <- c(77.967, -68.577)
times <- as.POSIXct("2026-12-21 00:00", tz = "Antarctica/Davis") + (0:23) * 3600
round(sun_position(times, lonlat[1], lonlat[2])$elevation, 1)
```

At local midnight on midsummer's day the sun is low in the south, and the hills throw long shadows:

```{r midnight}
p <- sun_position(as.POSIXct("2026-12-21 00:00", tz = "Antarctica/Davis"), lonlat[1], lonlat[2])
p
s <- cast_shade(vh, azimuth = p$azimuth, elevation = p$elevation, convergence = lonlat[1])
ximage(vh, col = relief, asp = 1, axes = FALSE)
ximage(s * 1, extent = attr(s, "extent"), add = TRUE, col = c("transparent", adjustcolor("midnightblue", 0.55)))
```

Over the whole day there are 24 hours of daylight. Terrain takes some of them away, most in the valleys
and on the slopes facing the pole:

```{r sun-hours}
h <- sun_hours(vh, date = "2026-12-21", lon = lonlat[1], lat = lonlat[2],
               tz = "Antarctica/Davis", step = 10, convergence = lonlat[1])
attr(h, "daylight")
summary(as.vector(h))
ximage(h, extent = attr(h, "extent"), col = hcl.colors(64, "Inferno"), asp = 1, axes = FALSE)
```

## Notes

- REMA is a surface model of snow, ice and rock. Over sea and sea ice it has no data, which is read as missing
  and treated as 0 m.
- The 20 m and 2 m grids here are resampled from REMA's 32 m and 2 m levels by GDAL's warper with bilinear
  resampling.
- The browser explorer for the same data source, with hillshade, profiles and per-level drill-down, is at
  <https://mdsumner.github.io/rema-ovr/>.
